• 2–6 players take turns on one device. A match lasts 1, 3 or 5 rounds.

• On your turn roll five dice. Then either keep them, or pick any of them and roll those once more.

• Hands from weakest to strongest: Nothing, One Pair, Two Pairs, Three of a Kind, Small Straight (1–5), Large Straight (2–6), Full House, Four of a Kind, Five of a Kind. Equal hands are decided by the higher dice.

• When everyone has played, the players are ranked by their hands. With N players the best hand earns N−1 points, each following place one point less and the last place 0. Identical hands share a place.

• A different player starts every round.

• The highest total after the last round wins. If first place is shared, the tied players play tiebreak rounds until one of them leads.

• 2–6 players take turns on one device.

• Before the game starts, choose whether it is played with one, two or three dice.

• In a duel every player rolls once. The highest total wins the duel and earns one win.

• If the highest total is shared, only the tied players roll again, until one of them wins.

• A different player rolls first in every duel. Play as many duels as you like.

• 2–6 players take turns on one device. A match lasts 1, 3 or 5 rounds.

• On your turn roll six dice. Every pair that adds up to 7 (1+6, 2+5, 3+4) is removed and scores nothing.

• After a roll either bank the sum of the dice still on the table, or roll those dice again. New pairs of 7 are removed as well.

• The player who opens a round may roll up to three times. Everyone else in that round may roll at most as many times as the opener did.

• If all six dice are removed, you score 0 for that turn.

• A different player opens every round. The highest total after the last round wins.
Pairs of dice that add up to 7 are removed and do not score
Tap the dice you want to roll again
